title: Lesson 21: William S. Hart and the Early Western Film
audio: /audio/nce4/21－William S. Hart and the Early Western Film.mp3

segments.text: Lesson 21
segments.translation: 第21课

segments.text: William S.Hart and the early 'Western' film
segments.translation: 威廉·S·哈特和早期的“西部片”

segments.text: Listen to the tape then answer this question.
segments.translation: 听录音，然后回答问题。

segments.text: How did William Hart's childhood prepare him for his acting role in Western films?
segments.translation: 威廉·哈特的童年经历如何为他在西方电影中的表演做好准备？

segments.text: William S.Hart was, perhaps, the greatest of all Western stars,
segments.translation: 威廉·S·哈特也许是所有西方明星中最伟大的，

segments.text: for unlike Gary Cooper and John Wayne he appeared in nothing but Westerns.
segments.translation: 因为与加里·库珀和约翰·韦恩不同，他只出现在西部片中。

segments.text: From 1914 to 1924 he was supreme and unchallenged.
segments.translation: 从1914年到1924年，他处于至高无上的地位，无人能挑战。

segments.text: It was Hart who created the basic formula of the Western film,
segments.translation: 是哈特创造了西部片的基本公式，

segments.text: and devised the protagonist he played in every film he made,
segments.translation: 并设计了他在每部电影中扮演的主角，

segments.text: the good-bad man, the accidental, noble outlaw,
segments.translation: 好人坏人，偶然的，高贵的亡命之徒，

segments.text: or the honest, but framed cowboy, or the sheriff made suspect by vicious gossip;
segments.translation: 或者是诚实但被陷害的牛仔，或者是因恶意八卦而受到怀疑的警长；

segments.text: in short, the individual in conflict with himself and his frontier environment.
segments.translation: 简而言之，个人与自己及其前沿环境发生冲突。

segments.text: Unlike most of his contemporaries in Hollywood,
segments.translation: 与好莱坞大多数同时代人不同，

segments.text: Hart actually knew something of the old West.
segments.translation: 哈特实际上对旧西部有所了解。

segments.text: He had lived in it as a child when it was already disappearing,
segments.translation: 当它已经消失时，他小时候就住在里面，

segments.text: and his hero was firmly rooted in his memories and experiences,
segments.translation: 他的英雄深深植根于他的记忆和经历中，

segments.text: and in both the history and the mythology of the vanished frontier,
segments.translation: 在消失的边疆的历史和神话中，

segments.text: And although no period or place in American history has been more absurdly romanticized,
segments.translation: 尽管美国历史上没有哪个时期或地方比这更荒谬地浪漫化了，

segments.text: myth and reality did join hands in at least one arena,
segments.translation: 神话和现实至少在一个舞台上携手共进，

segments.text: the conflict between the individual and encroaching civilization.
segments.translation: 个人与入侵文明之间的冲突。

segments.text: Men accustomed to struggling for survival against the elements and Indians
segments.translation: 习惯于与自然和印第安人抗争生存的男人

segments.text: were bewildered by politicians, bankers and businessmen,
segments.translation: 政客、银行家和商人都感到困惑，

segments.text: and unhorsed by fences, laws and alien taboos.
segments.translation: 并不受栅栏、法律和外来禁忌的束缚。

segments.text: Hart's good-bad man was always an outsider, always one of the disinherited,
segments.translation: 哈特笔下的好人和坏人总是一个局外人，总是一个被剥夺继承权的人，

segments.text: and if he found it necessary to shoot a sheriff or rob a bank along the way,
segments.translation: 如果他发现有必要在途中射杀治安官或抢劫银行，

segments.text: his early audiences found it easy to understand and forgive,
segments.translation: 他的早期观众发现它很容易理解和原谅，

segments.text: especially when it was Hart who, in the end, overcame the attacking Indians.
segments.translation: 尤其是当哈特最终战胜了进攻的印第安人时。

segments.text: Audiences in the second decade of the twentieth century
segments.translation: 二十世纪第二个十年的观众

segments.text: found it pleasant to escape to a time when life, though hard, was relatively simple.
segments.translation: 发现逃离到生活虽然艰难但相对简单的时代是件愉快的事。

segments.text: We still do; living in a world in which undeclared aggression, war, hypocrisy,
segments.translation: 我们仍然这样做；

segments.text: chicanery, anarchy and impending immolation are part of our daily lives,
segments.translation: 欺骗、无政府状态和即将发生的自焚是我们日常生活的一部分，

segments.text: we all want a code to live by.
segments.translation: 我们都想要一个赖以生存的准则。
